how-to-replace-text-in-pdf.h1: How to Replace Text in a PDF (Free, No Software)
how-to-replace-text-in-pdf.lead: A complete guide to editing text inside a PDF using a free online tool. Works on Windows, Mac, Linux, iPhone, and Android — all you need is a browser.

sections.h: Why editing PDFs is harder than editing Word docs
sections.p: PDFs lock text to absolute positions on the page so the layout never shifts. That makes them great for sharing and terrible for editing. Most desktop tools — including Adobe Acrobat — charge for the privilege. PDF Text Replace gives you the core feature for free in your browser.
Open the editor, click Upload, and pick your PDF. Files up to 25 MB are supported. Nothing is stored permanently — your file is auto-deleted within an hour.

sections.h: Step 2 — Enter the old and new text
sections.p: Type the exact text you want to find, then the replacement. Capitalisation matters. The tool searches every page and highlights every match in yellow.

sections.h: Step 3 — Choose which pages to edit
sections.p: Tick the page checkboxes for the pages you want changed. Leave the rest unchecked to keep them as-is. This is useful when, for example, only the cover page needs updating.
Click Replace & download. Your edited PDF is ready in seconds. Open it, check the result, and save it locally.
We've collected the most common questions in the FAQ on the homepage — including font preservation, image-based PDFs, and bulk replacements.

The site is supported by Google ads in the sidebar and between page previews. The ads pay for the servers so you don't have to. We never charge, never gate features behind a login, and never add a watermark.

sections.h: When this tool is the right choice
sections.p: Fixing a typo on the cover of a contract. Updating a date or address across a brochure. Re-using a quote template by swapping the client name. Translating a single line. The tool is purpose-built for these surgical edits.

If your PDF is a scanned image (no selectable text), the tool can't find the text — you'll need an OCR step first. If you need to redesign layout, swap fonts, or move objects around, you want a full PDF editor like Acrobat or a free alternative like LibreOffice Draw.
